purpose: Teach: 宝塚/グローブ/ジャンク/アリア/運勢/グレイ/悪人/グレン

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが宝塚歌劇に通われた
lines.en: You know, Gran — when your father was young, he used to go to the Takarazuka theatre all the time.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle voice, looking back through time. Slight pause before 'when your father was young' — retrieving an old memory. Warm but tinged with wistfulness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、野球のグローブを革で手入れされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and when you were young, you used to care for your baseball glove so carefully, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Light, teasing affection. Knowing smile in the voice. A playful counter-memory, gently turning the tables. Warm and present, not wistful — she's pulling him back to the room.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがコレクションのジャンクパーツを愛された
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he really loved collecting those old mechanical parts.
lines.style: Same wistful tone as before. Quieter this time. A gentle correction or continuation — he's offering another memory, not fighting hers. Slow, measured pace. Looking inward.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、オペラのアリアを口ずさまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And when you were young, you used to hum opera arias while you worked, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Brighter than before. She's not letting him drift too far into the past. Knowing, almost musical lilt on 'opera arias.' Affectionate but with a gentle insistence that his memories belong to her too.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが新聞の運勢欄を毎朝読まれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he'd read the fortune column in the newspaper every single morning.
lines.style: The wistfulness returns, deeper now. Voice drops slightly. Slower pace, as if this memory is smaller, more tender. A detail that mattered to him. Almost to himself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、グレイの三つ揃いスーツがお気に入りだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you looked so handsome in that grey three-piece suit when you were young, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, direct affection now. Not teasing — genuine admiration in the voice. She's meeting him eye-to-eye across the years. Soft but present. A small, certain smile.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが時代劇の悪人キャラ論評をされた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to analyze the villains in period dramas with such intensity.
lines.style: Wistful, but lighter. There's almost humor in this one — a quirk he's remembering fondly. Gentle rhythm. The kind of memory that makes you smile a little, even through the ache of missing someone.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、グレン・ミラーのスイングを愛されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you loved Glenn Miller's swing music so much when you were young, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Final memory. Warm, close, intimate. Her voice softens at the very end — 'didn't you dear' trails slightly, like she's savoring this last moment. A gentle closing, full of decades.
